Excellent! I now have a comprehensive understanding of the pipeline. Let me compile a thorough outline of the entire Bulk RNA-seq differential expression analysis pipeline for you. --- # 📋 Bulk RNA-seq Differential Expression Analysis — Complete Pipeline Outline Below is a comprehensive **end-to-end pipeline** covering raw reads to biological interpretation, incorporating all the tools you mentioned (STAR/HISAT2 for alignment, featureCounts for quantification, GO/KEGG enrichment). ```mermaid graph TD Start((Raw FASTQ)) --> QC1[FastQC: Pre-trim QC] QC1 --> Trim[Trim Galore! Adapter Trimming] Trim --> QC2[FastQC + MultiQC: Post-trim QC] QC2 --> Align{Alignment Strategy} Align -->|STAR| STAR_Align[[STAR: Spliced alignment]] Align -->|HISAT2| HISAT2_Align[[HISAT2: Hierarchical indexing alignment]] STAR_Align --> SortBAM1[samtools: Sort BAM] HISAT2_Align --> SortBAM2[samtools: Sort BAM] SortBAM1 --> Quant{Quantification Method} SortBAM2 --> Quant Quant -->|FeatureCounts| FC[[featureCounts: Gene-level counts]] Quant -->|HTSeq-count| HTSeq[[HTSeq-count: Gene-level counts]] Quant -->|Salmon/Sailfish| QuantTools[Salmon: Quasi-mapping quantification] FC --> CountMatrix[Gene Count Matrix] HTSeq --> CountMatrix QuantTools --> CountMatrix CountMatrix --> DE{Differential Expression} DE -->|DESeq2| DESeq2[[DESeq2: Negative binomial model]] DE -->|edgeR| edgeR[[edgeR: Exact test / GLM]] DE -->|limma-voom| Limma[[limma-voom: linear model + mean-variance]] DESeq2 --> DEGs[Significant DEGs
(padj<0.05, |log2FC|>1)] edgeR --> DEGs Limma --> DEGs DEGs --> Viz[Visualization] Viz --> Heatmap[Heatmap + PCA plot] Viz --> Volcano[Volcano plot] Viz --> MA[M/A plot] DEGs --> Enrich[Functional Enrichment Analysis] Enrich --> GO[GO Enrichment] GO --> BP[Biological Process] GO --> CC[Cellular Component] GO --> MF[Molecular Function] Enrich --> KEGG[KEGG Pathway Enrichment] KEGG --> Pathways[Pathway Maps] Enrich --> GSEA[[GSEA: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis
(uses all genes, no cutoff)]] GO --> Report((Final Report & Figures)) KEGG --> Report GSEA --> Report ``` --- ## 🔬 Phase 1: Quality Control (QC) ### Step 1.1 — Raw Data QC with **FastQC** - **Input**: Raw paired-end FASTQ files (`sample_R1.fastq.gz`, `sample_R2.fastq.gz`) - **Purpose**: Assess sequencing quality — per-base quality, GC content, adapter contamination, overrepresented sequences, duplication levels - **Command**: ```bash fastqc sample_R1.fastq.gz sample_R2.fastq.gz -o fastqc_raw/ ``` ### Step 1.2 — Adapter Trimming with **Trim Galore!** - **Input**: Raw FASTQ files - **Purpose**: Remove Illumina adapters, low-quality bases (Phred < 20), short reads (< 20 bp) - **Key parameters**: `-q 20` (quality cutoff), `--stringency 3`, `--paired` (paired-end mode) - **Command** (for paired-end): ```bash trim_galore -q 20 --phred33 --stringency 3 --length 20 \ --paired --gzip \ sample_R1.fastq.gz sample_R2.fastq.gz \ -o trim_galore_dir/ ``` - **Output**: Trimmed files (`sample_R1_val_1.fq.gz`, `sample_R2_val_2.fq.gz`) ### Step 1.3 — Post-trim QC with **FastQC + MultiQC** - Run FastQC again on trimmed files - Aggregate all QC reports using **MultiQC** for a unified HTML view ```bash multiqc fastqc_raw/ fastqc_trimmed/ -o multiqc_report/ ``` --- ## 🧬 Phase 2: Sequence Alignment ### Option A: **STAR** (Spliced Transcripts Alignment to a Reference) | Feature | STAR | |---------|------| | **Algorithm** | Suffix-array-based seed search + seed clustering + stitching | | **Speed** | ⚡ **Very fast** (8–10x faster than HISAT2 in most benchmarks) | | **Memory** | ~30 GB RAM for human genome | | **Splice Junctions** | ✅ De novo junction discovery | | **Best for** | High-coverage data, complex transcriptomes, speed-critical pipelines | **STAR key components:** 1. **Genome Index Generation** (one-time): ```bash STAR --runMode genomeGenerate \ --genomeDir star_index/ \ --genomeFastaFiles genome.fa \ --sjdbGTFfile annotations.gtf \ --runThreadN 16 ``` 2. **Alignment**: ```bash STAR --genomeDir star_index/ \ --readFilesIn sample_R1_val_1.fq.gz sample_R2_val_2.fq.gz \ --readFilesCommand zcat \ --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate \ --outFileNamePrefix sample_ \ --runThreadN 16 ``` ### Option B: **HISAT2** (Hierarchical Indexing for Spliced Alignment) | Feature | HISAT2 | |---------|--------| | **Algorithm** | Hierarchical FM-index (global + local indexes) | | **Speed** | Moderately fast | | **Memory** | ~5 GB RAM — much lower than STAR | | **Splice Junctions** | ✅ Supported via hierarchical indexing | | **Best for** | Resource-constrained environments, long-read RNA-seq | **HISAT2 key components:** 1. **Index Building** (one-time): ```bash hisat2-build genome.fa genome_tran # Or use hisat2_extract_splice_sites.py with GTF hisat2_extract_splice_sites.py annotations.gtf > splicesites.tsv hisat2_extract_exons.py annotations.gtf > exons.tsv hisat2-build --ss splicesites.tsv --exon exons.tsv genome.fa genome_tran ``` 2. **Alignment**: ```bash hisat2 -x genome_tran \ -1 sample_R1_val_1.fq.gz \ -2 sample_R2_val_2.fq.gz \ --threads 16 | \ samtools view -bS -F 4 | \ samtools sort -o sample_sorted.bam ``` **Comparison Summary:** | Criteria | ⭐ **STAR** | **HISAT2** | |----------|------------|------------| | Alignment Accuracy | 95–97% unique mapping | ~93–95% | | Speed (104M PE reads) | ~45 min | ~4.5 h | | RAM Usage | ~30 GB | ~4–5 GB | | Junction Discovery | Excellent (de novo) | Good (hierarchical) | | ENCODE/Pipeline Standard | ✅ Most widely recommended | ✅ Accepted alternative | --- ## 📊 Phase 3: Expression Quantification ### **featureCounts** (from subread package) — the preferred method - **Input**: Sorted BAM files + GTF annotation - **Purpose**: Count reads overlapping gene exons (gene-level quantification) - **Key parameters**: - `-p`: Paired-end reads - `-t exon`: Count exonic features - `-g gene_id`: Group by gene ID - `-s 0`: Unstranded (or `1` for stranded, `2` for reverse-stranded) - **Command**: ```bash featureCounts -p -t exon -g gene_id \ -a annotations.gtf \ -o counts.txt \ sample1_sorted.bam sample2_sorted.bam sample3_sorted.bam ``` - **Output**: `counts.txt` (gene-by-sample count matrix ready for downstream analysis) ### Alternative: **HTSeq-count** - Python-based, slower than featureCounts but equally robust ```bash htseq-count -f bam -r pos -s no \ sample_sorted.bam annotations.gtf > sample_counts.txt ``` --- ## 📈 Phase 4: Differential Expression Analysis ### Step 4.1 — Build Count Matrix - Merge all sample count files into a single matrix (genes × samples) - Rownames: Gene IDs; Columns: Sample conditions (Treatment vs Control) ### Step 4.2 — Choose a DE Tool | Tool | Model | Replicates | Best For | |------|-------|-------------|----------| | **DESeq2** | Negative Binomial + shrinkage | ≥2 per group | Small samples, dispersion shrinkage, robust | | **edgeR** | Negative Binomial + exact test/GLM | ≥2 per group | Fast on large data, flexible design | | **limma-voom** | Linear model + mean-variance weighting | ≥3 recommended | Complex designs, multifactorial experiments | **Example: DESeq2 Workflow in R** ```r library(DESeq2) # Read count matrix countdata <- read.table("counts.txt", header=TRUE, row.names=1) # Sample metadata (must have 'condition' column) coldata <- data.frame( condition = factor(c("Control","Control","Treatment","Treatment")) ) # Create DESeq dataset dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix( countData = countdata, colData = coldata, design = ~ condition ) # Run DESeq2 dds <- DESeq(dds) # Extract results res <- results(dds, contrast=c("condition","Treatment","Control")) res <- res[order(res$padj),] # Filter significant DEGs (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1) sig_degs <- subset(res, padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) > 1) write.csv(as.data.frame(sig_degs), "significant_DEGs.csv") ``` ### Step 4.3 — Diagnostic & Visualization Plots ```r # PCA Plot vsd <- vst(dds) plotPCA(vsd, intgroup="condition") # Volcano Plot with(res, plot(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), col = ifelse(padj<0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange)>1, "red", "black"), pch=20, main="Volcano Plot")) # Heatmap of top DEGs library(pheatmap) top_genes <- head(rownames(sig_degs), 50) pheatmap(assay(vsd)[top_genes,]) ``` --- ## 🧠 Phase 5: GO/KEGG Enrichment Analysis ### Step 5.1 — **GO Enrichment** (Gene Ontology) Using **clusterProfiler** in R — the gold-standard tool: ```r library(clusterProfiler) library(org.Hs.eg.db) # Human; use org.Mm.eg.db for mouse # Convert gene symbols to ENTREZ IDs deg_genes <- rownames(sig_degs) deg_entrez <- bitr(deg_genes, fromType="SYMBOL", toType="ENTREZID", OrgDb="org.Hs.eg.db") # GO Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) go_cc <- enrichGO(gene = deg_entrez$ENTREZID, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, ont = "CC", # Cellular Component pAdjustMethod = "BH", qvalueCutoff = 0.05) go_bp <- enrichGO(gene = deg_entrez$ENTREZID, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, ont = "BP", # Biological Process pAdjustMethod = "BH", qvalueCutoff = 0.05) go_mf <- enrichGO(gene = deg_entrez$ENTREZID, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, ont = "MF", # Molecular Function pAdjustMethod = "BH", qvalueCutoff = 0.05) # Visualization dotplot(go_bp, showCategory=15, title="GO Biological Process") barplot(go_cc, showCategory=15, title="GO Cellular Component") ``` ### Step 5.2 — **KEGG Pathway Enrichment** ```r # KEGG pathway over-representation test kegg <- enrichKEGG(gene = deg_entrez$ENTREZID, organism = "hsa", # "hsa" for human, "mmu" for mouse keyType = "kegg", pAdjustMethod = "BH", qvalueCutoff = 0.05) # Dotplot dotplot(kegg, showCategory=15, title="KEGG Pathway Enrichment") # Pathway map visualization browseKEGG(kegg, "hsa04110") # Opens KEGG map for specific pathway ``` ### Step 5.3 — **GSEA** (Gene Set Enrichment Analysis) — an alternative that uses **all genes** (no cutoff) ```r # Prepare gene list ranked by log2FC geneList <- res$log2FoldChange names(geneList) <- rownames(res) geneList <- sort(geneList, decreasing = TRUE) # GO GSEA gse_go <- gseGO(geneList = geneList, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, keyType = "SYMBOL", ont = "BP", minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 500, pvalueCutoff = 0.05) # KEGG GSEA gse_kegg <- gseKEGG(geneList = geneList, organism = "hsa", minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 500, pvalueCutoff = 0.05) # Running score plot gseaplot2(gse_kegg, geneSetID = 1, title = gse_kegg$Description[1]) ``` --- ## 🗺️ Complete Pipeline Workflow — Visual Summary ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Phase 1: QC" A[Raw FASTQ] --> B[FastQC] B --> C[Trim Galore!] C --> D[FastQC + MultiQC] end subgraph "Phase 2: Alignment" D --> E{Alignment Engine} E --> F[STAR
✓ Genome Generate
✓ Align Reads
✓ BAM Output] E --> G[HISAT2
✓ Index Build
✓ Spliced Align
✓ SAM→BAM] F --> H[samtools sort + index] G --> H end subgraph "Phase 3: Quantification" H --> I[featureCounts
✓ Read summarization
✓ Gene-level counts] I --> J[Gene Count Matrix] end subgraph "Phase 4: DE Analysis" J --> K[DESeq2 / edgeR / limma-voom] K --> L[Normalization
Dispersion
Statistical Test] L --> M[FDR Correction] M --> N[DEG Table
padj<0.05, |log2FC|>1] N --> O[PCA, Volcano,
Heatmap, MA-plot] end subgraph "Phase 5: Enrichment" N --> P{Enrichment Type} P --> Q[GO Enrichment
BP / CC / MF] P --> R[KEGG Pathway] P --> S[GSEA
All genes ranked] Q --> T[(Final Report)] R --> T S --> T end ``` --- ## 📚 Software & Key References | Tool | Reference | URL | |------|-----------|-----| | **FastQC** | Andrews S (2010) | babraham bioinformatics | | **Trim Galore!** | Krueger F | github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore | | **STAR** | Dobin et al. (2013) *Bioinformatics* | github.com/alexdobin/STAR | | **HISAT2** | Kim et al. (2019) *Nat Biotechnol* | daehwankimlab.github.io/hisat2 | | **featureCounts** | Liao et al. (2014) *Bioinformatics* | subread.sourceforge.net | | **DESeq2** | Love et al. (2014) *Genome Biology* | bioconductor.org | | **edgeR** | Robinson et al. (2010) *Bioinformatics* | bioconductor.org | | **limma** | Ritchie et al. (2015) *Nucleic Acids Res* | bioconductor.org | | **clusterProfiler** | Wu et al. (2021) *The Innovation* | bioconductor.org | | **MultiQC** | Ewels et al. (2016) *Bioinformatics* | multiqc.info | --- ## ✅ Key Decision Points Summary | Stage | Options | Our Recommendation | |-------|---------|-------------------| | **Aligner** | STAR vs HISAT2 | ⭐ **STAR** (faster, more accurate, ENCODE standard) | | **Quantification** | featureCounts vs HTSeq | ⭐ **featureCounts** (faster, simpler multi-sample) | | **DE Method** | DESeq2 / edgeR / limma | ⭐ **DESeq2** (best for typical 2-group, low-N setups) | | **Enrichment** | ORA vs GSEA | ⭐ **Both** — GSEA captures subtle coordinated changes | --- Would you like me to proceed to **Execution mode** so I can implement this pipeline on actual data? If you have specific FASTQ files or a dataset you'd like processed, I can help you set up the environment, prepare scripts, and run the entire workflow step by step.
